heading.en: Why maize beats wheat in the heat

hook.en: On a hot, bright day maize and sugarcane keep making sugar fast, while many C₃ plants waste energy. The secret is a CO₂ pump and a special leaf anatomy.
hook.kn: ಬಿಸಿ, ಪ್ರಕಾಶಮಾನ ದಿನದಲ್ಲಿ ಮೆಕ್ಕೆಜೋಳ ಮತ್ತು ಕಬ್ಬು ವೇಗವಾಗಿ ಸಕ್ಕರೆ ತಯಾರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ; ಅನೇಕ C₃ ಸಸ್ಯಗಳು ಶಕ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ವ್ಯರ್ಥ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಇದರ ರಹಸ್ಯ CO₂ ಪಂಪ್ ಮತ್ತು ವಿಶೇಷ ಎಲೆ ರಚನೆ.

title.en: Trace the Hatch and Slack pathway.

say.en: On a hot, bright day maize and sugarcane keep making sugar fast, while many C 3 plants waste energy. The secret is a CO 2 pump and a special leaf anatomy. In this lesson: Describe Kranz anatomy.
Trace the Hatch and Slack pathway.
Explain photorespiration and why C 4 plants avoid it.

body.en: C₄ plants, such as maize, sorghum and sugarcane, are adapted to dry tropical regions. Their leaves have Kranz anatomy (Kranz = wreath): large bundle sheath cells form several layers around the vascular bundles; they have a large number of chloroplasts, thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange, and no intercellular spaces. In the Hatch and Slack *pathway* the primary CO₂ acceptor is phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP), a 3-carbon molecule in the mesophyll cells, and the enzyme is PEP carboxylase (PEPcase). The first product is the 4-carbon oxaloacetic acid (OAA), which forms other 4-carbon acids such as malic or aspartic acid; these move to the bundle sheath cells and release CO₂ and a 3-carbon molecule. The 3-carbon molecule returns to the mesophyll to regenerate PEP. The released CO₂ enters the Calvin cycle in the bundle sheath cells, which are rich in RuBisCO but lack PEPcase; mesophyll cells lack RuBisCO.

points.en: C₄ acceptor: PEP (3C); first product: OAA (4C).
Calvin cycle runs in bundle sheath cells.
Kranz anatomy: big chloroplast-rich bundle sheath.

say.en: C 4 plants, such as maize, sorghum and sugarcane, are adapted to dry tropical regions. Their leaves have Kranz anatomy Kranz equals wreath: large bundle sheath cells form several layers around the vascular bundles; they have a large number of chloroplasts, thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange, and no intercellular spaces. In the Hatch and Slack pathway the primary CO 2 acceptor is phosphoenol pyruvate PEP, a 3-carbon molecule in the mesophyll cells, and the enzyme is PEP carboxylase PEPcase. The 3-carbon molecule returns to the mesophyll to regenerate PEP. The released CO 2 enters the Calvin cycle in the bundle sheath cells, which are rich in RuBisCO but lack PEPcase; mesophyll cells lack RuBisCO. C 4 acceptor: PEP 3C; first product: OAA 4C.

say.en: C₄ plants like maize show Kranz anatomy: large, chloroplast-rich bundle sheath cells in a ring around each vascular bundle.
In the mesophyll, PEP carboxylase fixes CO₂ onto PEP. The first product is oxaloacetic acid, a 4-carbon acid.
The C₄ acid moves to the bundle sheath and is decarboxylated. The CO₂ released there feeds RuBisCO and the Calvin cycle.
The 3-carbon pyruvate returns to the mesophyll and is turned back into PEP, ready for the next CO₂.
In C₃ plants RuBisCO can also bind O₂. Then RuBP gives one PGA and one phosphoglycolate, CO₂ is lost and no ATP or NADPH is made.

title.en: RuBisCO, oxygen and the C4 trick

caption.en: RuBisCO can bind O2 as well as CO2. When it binds O2 (photorespiration), no sugar is made and energy is wasted. Higher CO2 favours carboxylation; higher temperature favours oxygenation. C4 plants fix CO2 first with PEPcase in mesophyll cells and release it in bundle-sheath cells, raising CO2 around RuBisCO, so they almost avoid photorespiration. Illustrative numbers.
caption.kn: RuBisCO, CO2 ಜೊತೆಗೆ O2 ಅನ್ನೂ ಬಂಧಿಸಬಲ್ಲದು (ದ್ಯುತಿ ಉಸಿರಾಟ): ಸಕ್ಕರೆ ಇಲ್ಲ, ಶಕ್ತಿ ವ್ಯರ್ಥ. C4 ಸಸ್ಯಗಳು PEP ಕೇಸ್‌ನಿಂದ CO2 ಹಿಡಿದು ಬಂಡಲ್ ಶೀತ್ ಕೋಶಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ ಮಾಡಿ RuBisCO ಸುತ್ತ CO2 ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: RuBisCO, the most abundant enzyme in the world, can bind both CO₂ and O₂; its active site prefers CO₂ when CO₂ and O₂ are in equal amounts, and the relative concentration decides which one binds. In C₃ plants some O₂ binds RuBisCO, so instead of two PGA, RuBP + O₂ gives one PGA and one phosphoglycolate. This pathway, *photorespiration*, produces no sugar, no ATP and no NADPH; instead it releases CO₂ with the use of ATP, so it is wasteful. C₄ plants have no photorespiration because the C₄ pathway raises the CO₂ concentration at the RuBisCO site in the bundle sheath, so RuBisCO works as a carboxylase. Thus C₄ plants are more productive and tolerate higher temperatures.

points.en: No ATP or NADPH is made; CO₂ is released.

say.en: RuBisCO, the most abundant enzyme in the world, can bind both CO 2 and O 2; its active site prefers CO 2 when CO 2 and O 2 are in equal amounts, and the relative concentration decides which one binds. In C 3 plants some O 2 binds RuBisCO, so instead of two PGA, RuBP plus O 2 gives one PGA and one phosphoglycolate. This pathway, photorespiration, produces no sugar, no ATP and no NADPH; instead it releases CO 2 with the use of ATP, so it is wasteful. C 4 plants have no photorespiration because the C 4 pathway raises the CO 2 concentration at the RuBisCO site in the bundle sheath, so RuBisCO works as a carboxylase. Thus C 4 plants are more productive and tolerate higher temperatures. RuBP plus O 2 gives 1 PGA plus 1 phosphoglycolate.

problem.en: A leaf section shows wreath-like layers of large chloroplast-rich bundle sheath cells with thick walls. A ¹⁴CO₂ pulse shows label first in a 4-carbon acid. Identify the pathway, the primary acceptor, the first product and the site of the Calvin cycle.

steps.en: Wreath-like bundle sheath = Kranz anatomy, typical of C₄ plants.
The first labelled product is a 4C acid, oxaloacetic acid, formed from CO₂ + PEP by PEPcase in mesophyll cells.
The 4C acid releases CO₂ in the bundle sheath, where RuBisCO runs the Calvin cycle.

answer.en: C₄ (Hatch and Slack) pathway; PEP; OAA; bundle sheath cells

say.en: Let us work through this together. A leaf section shows wreath-like layers of large chloroplast-rich bundle sheath cells with thick walls. A to the power 14CO 2 pulse shows label first in a 4-carbon acid. Identify the pathway, the primary acceptor, the first product and the site of the Calvin cycle.
Wreath-like bundle sheath equals Kranz anatomy, typical of C 4 plants.
The first labelled product is a 4C acid, oxaloacetic acid, formed from CO 2 plus PEP by PEPcase in mesophyll cells.
The 4C acid releases CO 2 in the bundle sheath, where RuBisCO runs the Calvin cycle.
So the answer is C 4 Hatch and Slack pathway; PEP; OAA; bundle sheath cells.
